title: The Jelly Roll Morton band and sneaking drinks
summary: Punch tells how he and King Porter hid whiskey in a pot while the bandleader forbade drinking.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, head, humble, dream, all them kind of things. And I played with a, Jerry Roe Morton, but let me tell you the funny, now you're all going to laugh about this. Jerry didn't want no drinking. I went to Jerry, man, tall boy, tall boy, I call him King Porter, trumpet player, meaning I was playing first and I was playing second. So Porter hit me and said, look at you, I said, man, we can drink. I said, how are we going to drink, man? He said, I'll show you. Came into the saloon, man, we got a flash, each one's got a flash. Put it in the inside of the cook pot and get a straw, see, got a straw, put it in there, sunk that whiskey in there. So one guy, Jerry, says, something wrong with this band. Something wrong with this band. So we went out on the intermission, you know, and come back and old Jerry didn't come back with us, he's still up at the front door, you know, watching, you know. He was lying in and taking a zip to him and pulling, taking a zip, so Jerry come back and he wouldn't say nothing to us, he just hit me, he said, you got a half a pint, eh? And you got a half a pint. I said, I'm going to let you all move.
But he didn't fight, didn't he? He'd come on back to Chicago and he wouldn't take us out, you know. He didn't want no drinking. Strictly didn't want no drinking.
Mr. Porter, did he write King Porter Stone?
Yeah, yeah, yeah. King Porter, he wrote Royal Garden Blues. And what that thing, uh... Black Bottom. He wrote all them general.
I was crazy about that Royal Garden Blues. Whoo!
